headline: The H3 pipeline is already architected as DiT-resident with on-demand encoder and VAEs. That reframes rounds 117-119 and forces a correction: round 76's 13.62 s decode was a WARM SECOND request with the VAE already loaded, while its cold first request decoded in 128.27 s - so decode cost is dominated by on-demand VAE weight loading, not by decoder compute.
why_this_round: Round 119 concluded the DiT-resident-plus-resident-VAE configuration is unreachable and pointed at load-time staging. This round read the actual pipeline offload plan instead of guessing, to find where the residency decisions are made.

pipeline_architecture_as_found.class: MiniMaxH3Pipeline, current patched file dated 2026-11-16, with local patch backups present (agbak, decodefp16, decodesplit, teblock, teondemand, pre_round64_20261116)

offload_plan.resident_dit_paths: frozenset({'transformer'}) - the DiT is RESIDENT by design
offload_plan.on_demand_component_paths: frozenset({'text_encoder', 'video_vae', 'audio_vae'}) - the encoder and both VAEs are loaded ON DEMAND

pipeline_architecture_as_found.conditional_wiring: load_text_encoder controls whether the encoder is loaded at all: when False the encoder block attrs, the on_demand path and the encode_prompt profiler target are all removed; load_vae_encoder independently gates _encode_local_media
pipeline_architecture_as_found.significance: there is no 'DiT resident vs offloaded' choice to make - the DiT is always resident in this stack. What varies between my runs is whether the ENCODER is present, and the VAE is always on-demand.

component_sizes_measured.note: measured with du on the host; the deployed model path /tmp/h3_round53_native49_fp16_model symlinks these exact directories
component_sizes_measured.dit_per_rank_measured: 10.4337 GiB, from the round-119 load log 'Model loading took 10.4337 GiB'
component_sizes_measured.steady_state_weights_if_all_resident: roughly 20 GiB per rank, which would fit in 32 GiB, so the round-119 OOM at 31.3 GiB during VAE shard loading is a load-time transient

correction_to_round_118.what_round_118_said: decode is 13.62 s when resident versus about 468 s offloaded, a 34x collapse attributed to the VAE being swapped in per decode
correction_to_round_118.what_is_actually_true: round 76 reported 128.27 s of decode on its COLD FIRST request and 13.62 s on its WARM SECOND request in the same process. The 13.62 s therefore already had the VAE loaded and reused, and about 115 s of the cold request was VAE on-demand loading.
correction_to_round_118.why_this_matters: the decode penalty is mostly the cost of loading 9.8 GiB of VAE weights on demand rather than a property of the decoder kernel, and the relevant comparison for a single cold request is 128.27 s, not 13.62 s
correction_to_round_118.what_survives: the direction of round 118's conclusion is intact - decode cost is dominated by weight residency, not arithmetic - but its magnitude for a single request was overstated and is corrected here

residency_pressure_explained.round_116_encoder_live: DiT resident 10.43 GiB + encoder present (77 blocks, rank-local layerwise) + VAE on-demand load: 33.45 s/step and a decode-plus-residual of 472.1 s
residency_pressure_explained.round_76_text_encoder_false: DiT resident with NO encoder in the process: 14.657 s/step, cold decode 128.27 s, warm decode 13.62 s
residency_pressure_explained.difference: the encoder's presence is what costs both the per-step time and the decode time; the VAE loading cost is unavoidable in either mode because the VAE is on-demand by design
residency_pressure_explained.round_119_attempt: disabling the DiT from being offloaded was a misreading of the architecture - the DiT was never offloaded in the sense I assumed; the run still failed while loading the VAE on top of the resident DiT and a present encoder

actionable_conclusion: The lever for decode is to stop paying the 9.8 GiB VAE load on every request: keep the VAE resident between requests (it already stays loaded within one process - that is exactly why round 76's second request decoded in 13.62 s), or reduce the VAE's footprint/transfer cost.
The lever for the per-step cost is the encoder's residency, which round 116 measured at 2.28x - and which production avoids by encoding before the DiT loop.
Both levers are scheduling/residency questions, not kernel questions, which is consistent with rounds 115 and 117.

For the comparable measurement, a staged run that loads the encoder once, encodes, releases it, then serves denoise plus decode with a warm VAE is the configuration that matches how an operator would actually deploy this.
not_claimed: no single-run staged end-to-end measurement yet
next: Run staged mode end to end in ONE process with two requests, so the second request has a warm VAE: that single run yields the comparable per-step, decode and total figures without composition or cold-start contamination.
Measure the VAE on-demand load time directly by timing the first versus second decode in the same process.
Only after those, revisit whether the load-time transient can be shrunk enough to avoid VAE eviction entirely.
